metadata.description: Compute Kalshi noise floor — how much directional error is Kalshi noise vs signal error

era5_vs_kalshi.interpretation: ERA5 (reanalysis) vs Kalshi settlements has MAE of 2.91°F. This is the Kalshi noise floor — even perfect model-information about the weather can't do better than ±2.91°F because Kalshi itself has measurement noise.

multi_model_consensus.interpretation: Multi-model (ECMWF+GEM+GFS+ICON) consensus vs Kalshi has MAE of 9.28°F. This is the NWP noise floor — averaging multiple models barely beats ERA5.

directional_noise_floor.interpretation: Kalshi settlements disagree with ERA5 reanalysis on temperature direction 22.3% of the time. This means ~22% of our "directional errors" may actually be Kalshi noise, not model error. When they disagree, the mean Kalshi temp shift is 3.1°F, suggesting small-magnitude direction changes are the most noise-prone.

effective_ceiling.observation: Even ERA5 reanalysis (perfect model) gets direction right only 77.7% of the time against Kalshi settlements. This is the KALSHI NOISE FLOOR on directional accuracy. The remaining 22% is Kalshi measurement noise, microclimate, NWP grid-cell averaging error, and temporal sampling mismatch.
